markdown_report:
The next experiment should complete the exported-predictor audit before changing BERT4Rec training. At 30% progress, this resolves a documented uncertainty with bounded computation and no additional fitting.

**Insights from the supplied evidence**

1. All four categories pass four live inference fixtures with zero reported score discrepancy. This supports those live paths but leaves exported checkpoint, mapping and routing consistency unresolved.
2. Movies user 8675 has training-recovery catalog rank 425 yet expected sampled HR@10 of 0.999856. Candidate-set effects explain this coexistence; it does not establish an implementation fault or held-out improvement.
3. Margin probes inspected zero batches, while provenance and deployment checks remain unavailable. Missing observations identify integration gaps rather than evidence of failed supervision.

**Insights from related work**

1. The supplied [metamorphic-testing study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156) motivates checking predictable transformations. Its results do not validate this proposed BERT4Rec fault suite.
2. [PyTorch checkpoint guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html) motivates immutable selected-state snapshots and explicit reloads. Artifact identity therefore needs a separate check even when rankings agree.
3. [RecTools](https://rectools.readthedocs.io/en/stable/examples/tutorials/transformers_tutorial.html) documents appended-mask inference. Short, unequally left-padded histories are useful fixtures for exposing an incorrect count−1 readout.

Three directions follow: establish deployment identity, calibrate behavioral checks, then investigate history dependence. Their conceptual map separates evidence layers:

| Layer | Question | Present gap |
|---|---|---|
| Consumed training | Were targets and loss constructed correctly? | Missing captures |
| Exported inference | Does deployment implement the selected checkpoint? | Unverified parity |
| Recommendation quality | Does ranking generalize? | Requires pinned validation |

Three atomic ideas are feasible. Scores below are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Artifact identity gate — 3/7/3.** Originality: useful integration, established hashing. Potential: catches stale exports, cannot certify computation. Difficulty: compact manifest, needs actual load instrumentation.
- **Fault-calibrated export replay — 5/8/6; selected.** Originality: connects routing, masking and ranking checks, uses established differential testing. Potential: localizes deployment faults, cannot directly improve preferences. Difficulty: requires no retraining, needs independent reconstruction and verified mutations.
- **Position-preserving history substitutions — 5/7/5.** Originality: combines frequency controls and positional interventions, extends familiar perturbations. Potential: motivates masking changes, measures dependence rather than intent. Difficulty: reuses scoring, matching availability and semantics is demanding.

For the selected idea, freeze the selected artifacts, reconstruct canonical inputs independently, and invoke the actual exported predictor in a fresh process. Compare identity, tokens, finite scores, rankings and bounded full-catalog unseen-item selection. Calibrate using verified routing, identity, mapping, mask and readout faults plus harmless controls. Report unsupported instrumentation as unavailable. Preserve one trained BERT4Rec checkpoint/category and all benchmark settings; only unchanged host macro validation HR@10 selects revisions.

idea.description: Implement a bounded, fault-calibrated differential audit of the actual exported working/predict.py against an independently reconstructed reference loaded from the same selected BERT4Rec checkpoint. Separately assess artifact identity, category routing, input construction, candidate scores, ranking and simulator selection. Reference reloads are audit executions of identical trained parameters, never additional fitted predictors or sources of fused recommendations.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics establish agreement on bounded live fixtures but explicitly leave fresh-process export parity unverified. Training-recovery examples also demonstrate that sampled and catalog outcomes can differ predictably. A deployment audit addresses the unresolved implementation boundary without interpreting candidate-set effects, embedding alignment or qualitative feedback as evidence of a model defect or validation gain.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an integration specification: executable replacement training code cannot be grounded in the supplied workflow summary alone. Instrument the existing predictor writer and actual exported entry point; do not substitute a diagnostic reimplementation for the production path.

After checkpoint selection, freeze a trial-local manifest containing category, checkpoint-byte hash, canonical ordered item-map hash, architecture configuration, reserved IDs, sequence length and exported source hash. Hashes establish identity relative to this manifest, not independent authenticity. Instrument actual artifact loading to report resolved paths and hashes; a runner that only echoes expected manifest values does not certify loading. Verify all four routes. Load exactly one selected independently trained checkpoint per category for production prediction. Execute reference and exported audit runs sequentially on CPU where supported to bound resource use; neither run contributes additional production scores.

Independently construct left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK], L). The readout is the final nonpadding absolute position, L-1 for this construction. Use empty, short, unequal-padding, repeated-item and truncation-boundary fixtures. Reserved-mask supervision and bidirectional BERT4Rec remain unchanged. Compare exact canonical token and candidate IDs where actual-path tracing exists. Without tracing, report input/readout internals as unverified even if scores agree.

Call the actual exported predictor in a fresh process through its existing public interface. Preserve its candidate ordering, output semantics and scoring function. Require finite outputs before filtering. Record maximum absolute error, stabilized relative error with its denominator floor, and tolerance-pass counts; predeclare FP32 starting tolerances rtol=1.3e-6 and atol=1e-5. Precision differences require explicit reporting, not retrospective tolerance tuning. Report ordered top-10 equality, set overlap and target-rank agreement separately. Use the deployed tie policy; if unspecified, report tie ambiguity rather than asserting a common ordering.

Predeclare at most eight fixtures/category and a fixed process timeout. For the twenty designated training users, audit the actual native full-catalog unseen-item selection with their existing contexts and filtering rules. Stream reference scores under a recorded chunk policy and compare returned IDs, uniqueness, seen-item exclusions, reserved-token exclusions and ordered selection. Report numerical near-tie discrepancies separately. Do not manufacture a target or HR metric for these recommendations. Stop at the predeclared runtime cap, recording incomplete users and unavailable comparisons.

On isolated copies only, inject five faults: wrong category route, incorrect checkpoint identity, one-sided item-map permutation, omitted appended mask and count−1 readout. An alternative checkpoint must be a disposable altered copy of the current artifact, never another trial's checkpoint. Independently verify that each injection changes the intended property; distinguish invalid, inapplicable, equivalent and unresolved injections. Identity faults must fail the identity gate even if fixture scores coincide. Numerical faults need not be detected on every behaviorally insensitive fixture.

Controls include unchanged fresh reload, batch reorder/splitting and candidate reorder followed by inverse permutation, where supported. Check control preconditions independently. Report detected/verified non-equivalent faults and false alarms/verified harmless controls with explicit denominators; zero denominators are null. These bounded rates do not estimate real fault prevalence.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all supplied ModelView hooks. Add optional export-runner and manifest transport without changing B×L diagnostic tuples. Missing transport yields null with a reason. Preserve existing probes and do not advance the production loader. Restore module modes, main-process RNG and changed precision settings in finally. Record measured cost, completion and failures against the shared budget.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per completed epoch. No extra data, pretrained weights, independent scorers, averaging or score fusion. Only pinned host macro validation HR@10 selects revisions. Passing the audit establishes bounded deployment consistency, not convergence, immediate user choice or held-out gains.

originality.positive: Combines actual exported execution, artifact identity and verified fault calibration across the specific BERT4Rec deployment boundaries.
originality.negative: Differential testing, manifests and mutation testing are established; novelty lies in their task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable deployment gate and localizes discrepancies before subsequent single-model learning experiments.
future_potential.negative: Bounded agreement cannot certify every execution path or directly improve validation ranking and recommendation usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no additional fitting or architecture change and supports tightly bounded fixture execution.
code_difficulty.negative: Actual-path instrumentation, independent reference construction, subprocess isolation and verified mutation accounting require substantial integration.

related_work.title: 2024 empirical study of metamorphic testing for recommender systems
contributions: The supplied search summary reports six metamorphic relations evaluated across LibRec, PREA and Surprise.
Motivates checking predictable transformations when complete output oracles are unavailable.
limitations: Does not independently validate the proposed BERT4Rec deployment mutations.
Harmless transformations require explicit preconditions for the actual predictor interface.

related_work.title: PyTorch: Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Documents checkpoint reload and evaluation-mode practices.
Explains the mutable best-state reference pitfall relevant to selected-checkpoint identity.
limitations: Does not certify item mappings, category routing or exported recommendation behavior.

related_work.title: RecTools transformer tutorial
contributions: Provides a documented precedent for BERT4Rec appended-mask inference.
limitations: Does not establish correctness of this host's predictor writer or left-padding readout.

related_work.title: PyTorch ONNX export verification documentation
contributions: Provides a precedent for numerical comparison between reference and exported execution.
limitations: Numerical agreement alone does not establish ranking agreement near ties.
The proposed Python predictor audit does not require or assume ONNX conversion.
